visual_text: “Loneliness is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day”
Claim as widely repeated; not a finding of this post
How involved people were with others
The chart set numbers from different reviews of different people beside smoking fewer than 15 cigarettes a day.
A study of about 6,500 people aged 52 and over in England
After allowing for age and health at the start

In this one study, social isolation was still linked with death and loneliness was not clearly linked. Larger reviews still link loneliness with a higher risk of dying, less strongly than isolation. We should still act on loneliness, because it is painful to live with.
Steptoe et al., PNAS, 2013 (observational, about 7 years of follow-up)
alt_text: Text card. The popular claim in quotation marks: loneliness is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Below it: where does the comparison appear? The card says this is a widely repeated claim and not a finding of this post.

Card on what the 2010 review measured: 148 studies, about 309,000 people. Most results measured marriage and living alone, social networks, support and involvement with others. Loneliness: 8 results. The chart set numbers from different reviews beside smoking fewer than 15 cigarettes a day.

Card on about 6,500 people aged 52 and over in England. After allowing for age and health, social isolation was still linked with death and loneliness was not clearly linked. Larger reviews still link loneliness with higher risk of dying. The card says we should still act on loneliness because it is painful.
